info.name: Hierarchy-aware list filter matrix (Slice 5.5-B)
info.description: Proves the hierarchy-aware LIST filter end to end through the gateway: an ancestor (Catalog) grant WIDENS a category list to the whole catalog subtree (rows the subject's own leaf-tags would never surface), two subjects on the SAME endpoint get DIFFERENT row sets, a leaf abac_deny still REMOVES a row from the widened list, and an unbound stranger gets []. The re-parent move (a row leaving one subject's widened list) is done by the runner between two passes of this collection (phase=pre|post) — the same ltree subtree rewrite CatalogHierarchyService.reparentCategory does. The decisive contrast is the row SET, not a single 200/403.

item.name: E1 — Inherit reader lists categories -> WIDENED to the whole catalog subtree

exec: pm.test('200 OK (the coarse list gate let the inheritable grant through)', () => pm.response.code === 200);
const ids = pm.response.json().items.map(c => c.id);
const phase = pm.variables.get('phase');
// The inherit reader has NO category tag grant; it sees these rows ONLY because the Catalog grant
// widens the list to the whole catalog subtree (the headline).
pm.test('sees the EMEA category (in the subtree)', () => pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.variables.get('emea_category_id')));
if (phase === 'pre') {
pm.test('PRE-reparent: sees the APAC category (in the subtree, NOT by its own tags)', () => pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.variables.get('apac_category_id')));
} else {
pm.test('POST-reparent: the moved APAC category LEFT catalog C\'s widened list', () => pm.expect(ids).to.not.include(pm.variables.get('apac_category_id')));
pm.test('does NOT see the DENIED category (deny-overrides)', () => pm.expect(ids).to.not.include(pm.variables.get('deny_category_id')));

item.name: E2 — Region reader lists categories -> only the EMEA row (DIFFERENT set, same endpoint)

exec: pm.test('200 OK', () => pm.response.code === 200);
const ids = pm.response.json().items.map(c => c.id);
// The region reader is tag-gated to region=emea (and has its own category:read), so it sees only
// the emea row via the residual — NOT the apac row the inherit reader sees pre-reparent. A different cut.
pm.test('sees the EMEA category', () => pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.variables.get('emea_category_id')));
pm.test('does NOT see the APAC category (its tags do not match)', () => pm.expect(ids).to.not.include(pm.variables.get('apac_category_id')));
pm.test('does NOT see the DENIED category', () => pm.expect(ids).to.not.include(pm.variables.get('deny_category_id')));

item.name: E4 — Stranger (no role definition) lists categories -> EMPTY / 403 (fail-closed)

exec: // The unbound stranger resolves NO role definition, so neither the coarse list gate (no inheritable
// grant) nor the SQL filter (no role -> DENY_ALL residual) lets any row through. 403 at the gate OR
// 200 with an empty body are both fail-closed; assert NO category is visible either way.
pm.test('fail-closed: 403 at the gate, or 200 with an empty list', () => pm.expect([200, 403]).to.include(pm.response.code));
if (pm.response.code === 200) {
const ids = pm.response.json().items.map(c => c.id);
pm.test('sees NO categories (empty, not the whole table)', () => pm.expect(ids.length).to.eql(0));
